audit_findings.title: OneOncology perimeter is internally stale after the acquisition completed
audit_findings.magnitude: filed consideration $7,387.1 million; debt increased $4,062.5 million from 2025-09-30 to 2026-06-30; nine-month net interest expense increased $139.9 million year over year; acquired OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor omits acquired earnings, incremental interest, integration costs, NCI and purchase-accounting effects, while the bridge uses the post-acquisition balance sheet.
audit_findings.evidence: TPG owns a put option that, beginning on the third anniversary of the closing and ending on the day before the fourth anniversary of the closing, allows it to require the Company to purchase the remaining interests in the joint venture at a price equal to 19 times OneOncology EBITDA, subject to various adjustments and qualifications.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible risk. OneOncology closed on February 2, 2026, before the valuation date, and the latest filing already consolidates its results. The omitted acquired earnings could increase value, while financing, integration, NCI and other burdens could reduce it. The transaction and financing are large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun from post-closing results or a disciplined pro forma including OneOncology OE, incremental interest, integration costs, purchase-accounting effects, physician notes, retained equity/NCI and all acquisition funding.

audit_findings.title: The $4.3 billion opioid settlement liability is a senior cash claim omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: latest filed liability $4.2 billion, including $396.2 million due within 12 months; gross amount equals 9.6% of $43,774 million base equity value or $21.81 per diluted share; after-tax present value unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future settlement payments consume equity cash but generally do not re-enter net income after the liability has already been accrued; absent an OE deduction, the claim belongs in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The $ 4.3 billion liability will be paid over 13 years.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its omission from the stated bridge are demonstrated. The filed cash claim is materially larger than the entire $2,846.5 million cash add-back. The precise valuation adjustment remains unresolved because the payment schedule, tax deductions and any amounts already captured in projected OE must be traced.
audit_findings.action: Map the remaining settlement schedule into projected OE and subtract the after-tax present value from the bridge to the extent payments are not already deducted; separately evaluate unaccrued opioid matters without assigning an unsupported amount.

audit_findings.title: RCA contingent and physician-equity liabilities may sit ahead of common equity without a bridge deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: latest filed liabilities $957.6 million for equity units plus $412.6 million for business objectives, totaling $1,370.2 million; this equals 3.1% of base equity value or $7.11 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement would require a bridge deduction; equity settlement would affect fully diluted shares; recurring physician-option compensation must remain in OE if not reflected through either route.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s estimated liability related to the equity units is $ 815.2 million and is recorded in Other Liabilities on the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheet, as of September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The liabilities and absence of an explicit bridge adjustment are demonstrated, but their incremental valuation effect is unresolved. The record does not establish settlement form, timing or how much related compensation was retained in the OE anchor. Consequently, a material common-equity burden is possible, but the current record cannot establish the proper deduction without risking double counting.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the RCA unit agreements and payment timetable, classify each obligation as cash, equity or recurring compensation, then rerun the bridge, diluted share count and OE consistently while reconciling the $121.7 million FY2025 and $143.6 million nine-month FY2026 expenses.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include operating liquidity rather than distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,846.5 million cash add-back, equal to 6.5% of base equity value or $14.78 per diluted share; largest nine-month fiscal 2026 intra-period borrowings were $6.8 billion; required operating-cash portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required to finance ordinary working-capital timing supports the valued operating earnings and cannot also be added to the equity bridge as excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The largest amount of intra-period borrowings under our revolving and securitization credit facilities that was outstanding at any one time during fiscal 2025 and 2024 was $5.1 billion and $3.2 billion, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash add-back and heavy intra-period funding requirement are demonstrated, but neither proves how much cash is permanently required. The potential exposure is material in scale, while the actual excess-cash amount cannot be established from period-end balances or maximum borrowings alone.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum unrestricted operating cash from daily or monthly working-capital balances, supplier-payment timing, borrowing peaks, restricted cash and acquisition flows, then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Forward owner earnings may understate required capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: fiscal 2026 expected capex $900.0 million versus fiscal 2025 actual $668.0 million, a $232.0 million increase equal to 9.4% of the $2,468.9 million OE anchor; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring maintenance and compliance capex reduces forward OE before growth is applied; growth capex must be matched with the growth it supports.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to spend approximately $900 million on capital expenditures during fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher spending plan is filed and applies to the valuation's initial projection period, but the record does not separate maintenance, compliance and expansion spending. Therefore the $232.0 million difference cannot automatically be treated as a permanent OE reduction, although its scale could materially affect value if substantially recurring.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the fiscal 2026 capex breakdown and asset-replacement plan, identify the recurring maintenance and compliance component, and rerun forward OE with that component deducted before applying scenario growth.

audit_findings.title: Antitrust recoveries could inflate normalized operating earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: filed pretax gains were $239.1 million in 2023, $170.9 million in 2024 and $236.4 million in 2025, totaling $646.4 million; nine-month 2026 gains fell to $34.2 million; effect retained in the OE anchor unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If included in reported earnings used for the OE series, litigation recoveries raise the trend anchor and are then compounded by growth and terminal capitalization despite lacking demonstrated durability.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023, the Company recognized gains relating to these lawsuits of $ 236.4 million, $ 170.9 million, and $ 239.1 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The recoveries and their earnings classification are demonstrated, but the supplied OE reconciliation does not establish whether they were removed. Their sharp decline in fiscal 2026 supports treating them separately from durable operating economics. Materiality remains unresolved until their inclusion and tax effect in each OE observation are traced.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to filed earnings, identify the after-tax amount of antitrust gains retained, and rerun the trend anchor excluding those gains or modeling a separately supported, non-growing recovery stream.
